inlines.text: Anthropic

blocks.text: 非营利组织METR获得了为期十一周的权限，得以接触Anthropic的内部研究数据。其结论是：Anthropic模型的提升速度大约翻了一倍，而其中约80%的加速可追溯到AI被用于公司自身的研究。不过，Anthropic对最重要的证据做了涂黑处理。

inlines.text: 非营利组织METR获得了为期十一周的权限，得以接触Anthropic的内部研究数据。其结论是：Anthropic模型的提升速度大约翻了一倍，而其中约80%的加速可追溯到AI被用于公司自身的研究。不过，Anthropic对最重要的证据做了涂黑处理。

blocks.text: AI是否正在加速更优AI的开发，被视为安全讨论中的一个关键早期预警信号。人们担心会形成一种反馈回路：模型越来越快地改进自己的后继者，而据METR称，这可能导致“极端且危险的能力突然涌现”。Anthropic在其负责任扩展政策中正是把这类加速列为风险指标：如果AI的进步速度因自动化AI研究而翻倍，就应触发警告级别。

blocks.text: 这正是METR想要验证的。这家非营利组织研究的课题之一，是AI开发者是否可能失去对自家系统的控制。2026年8月12日至10月29日，一支相当于2.5名全职人员的团队获得了他们所称的“前所未有的权限”，可以查看未发布模型的基准测试结果、训练指标、员工调查和内部分析，并对Anthropic的研究人员进行了约15次访谈。METR没有收取Anthropic的任何费用，但出于安全考虑，工作是在Anthropic的设备上进行的。

blocks.text: 两年的进展压缩进一年

inlines.text: 两年的进展压缩进一年

blocks.text: 据METR称，自2025年10月以来，Anthropic模型测试分数的攀升速度约为2024年3月至2025年10月期间的1.9倍。这一衡量基于AECI，一个将多项基准测试打包在一起的综合指标。Anthropic用一年时间取得了此前需要两年才能实现的进展，大致相当于从Claude 2.1到Sonnet 4.5的跃升。分析还纳入了三个于2026年7月至10月间完成训练的未发布模型。2025年10月之前，Anthropic的模型每年约提升15个AECI点；此后，这一速度达到了29。

blocks.text: METR确信，这一加速并非由训练算力增长加快所驱动。相反，审计人员估计，当前约80%的提速来自AI被用于Anthropic自身的研究。一位员工在访谈中说：“现在瓶颈只在想法和算力上，不再卡在代码上了。”

blocks.text: 目前 AI 还做不到完全自主研究。加速主要来自 AI 充当助手，但已经出现“生命迹象”，独立贡献可能很快发挥更大作用。METR 没有发现会在未来十二个月拖慢节奏的瓶颈，这意味着加速在未来一年继续扩大的“风险很大”。

blocks.text: 巨大的不确定性与异议声音

inlines.text: 巨大的不确定性与异议声音

blocks.text: METR 也强调结果有多不精确。真实的加速系数可能低至 1.3，也可能高达 3。把 OpenAI、Google 和 xAI 的模型算进来后，全行业的数字降到只有 1.4，可能是因为 Anthropic 在 2025 年落后于竞争对手，追赶效应扭曲了数据。

blocks.text: Anthropic 内部的观点也不统一。一位研究员认为 AI 在生产力提升中的贡献只占 15% 到 20%，并且不信任同事的自我报告。另一位则认为新员工是近几个月最重要的单一因素。

blocks.text: 被删减的证据削弱了审计

inlines.text: 被删减的证据削弱了审计

blocks.text: Anthropic 对所有非公开信息拥有单方面的删减权，并且大量行使了这一权利。据 METR 称，审计人员评为信息量最大的证据大部分被删掉了，包括对未来模型的预测、按训练步骤的细分以及瓶颈分析。Anthropic 称这些删减“旨在移除可能加速其他 AI 开发者的机密信息”。

blocks.text: Anthropic 叫停了算力分配审计

inlines.text: Anthropic 叫停了算力分配审计

blocks.text: 在另一份评审中，METR 还审视了 Anthropic 2026 年 8 月的风险报告。在那份报告里，公司公开表示加速“不到 2 倍”。但内部未删减版本暗示数值为 1.97，而 Anthropic 自己也称阈值被突破是“有可能的”。METR 认为警告级别可能在 7 月 15 日就已经达到，并指责公开报告既低估了加速程度，也低估了围绕它的不确定性。

blocks.text: Anthropic

inlines.text: Anthropic

blocks.text: Nonprofit METR got eleven weeks of access to Anthropic's internal research data. Its finding: the rate at which Anthropic's models are improving has roughly doubled, and about 80 percent of that acceleration traces back to AI being used in the company's own research. Anthropic redacted the most important evidence, though.

inlines.text: Nonprofit METR got eleven weeks of access to Anthropic's internal research data. Its finding: the rate at which Anthropic's models are improving has roughly doubled, and about 80 percent of that acceleration traces back to AI being used in the company's own research. Anthropic redacted the most important evidence, though.

blocks.text: Whether AI is speeding up the development of better AI is considered a key early warning signal in the safety debate. The concern is that a feedback loop could form where models improve their successors faster and faster, which according to METR could lead to a "sudden emergence of extreme and risky capabilities." Anthropic flags exactly this kind of acceleration as a risk indicator in its Responsible Scaling Policy: if the pace of AI progress doubles because of automated AI research, that should trigger a warning level.

blocks.text: That's what METR set out to verify. The nonprofit studies, among other things, whether AI developers could lose control of their systems. From August 12 to October 29, 2026, a team of 2.5 full-time staffers received what they describe as unprecedented access to benchmark results from unreleased models, training metrics, employee surveys, and internal analyses, along with roughly 15 interviews with Anthropic researchers. METR took no money from Anthropic but worked on Anthropic devices for security reasons.

blocks.text: Two years of progress packed into one

inlines.text: Two years of progress packed into one

blocks.text: Since October 2025, Anthropic's model test scores have been climbing about 1.9 times faster than they did between March 2024 and October 2025, according to METR. The measurement is based on the AECI, a composite metric that bundles many benchmarks together. Anthropic achieved in one year what previously took two, roughly comparable to the jump from Claude 2.1 to Sonnet 4.5. The analysis also included three unreleased models that finished training between July and October 2026. Before October 2025, Anthropic's models gained about 15 AECI points per year; since then, the rate has hit 29.

blocks.text: METR is confident the acceleration isn't driven by faster growth in training compute. Instead, the auditors estimate that about 80 percent of the current speedup comes from AI being used in Anthropic's own research. One employee said in the interviews: "Now only bottlenecked on ideas & compute, no longer bottlenecked on code."

blocks.text: Others reported that experiments that used to take one to two days to set up are now "~free." In informal Slack polls from October 2026, employees said on average that the latest internal model made them roughly twelve times more productive. METR treats these self-assessments as "very loose evidence," calling them unrepresentative and likely to overstate the actual gains.

blocks.text: AI isn't doing fully autonomous research yet. The acceleration comes mainly from AI acting as an assistant, but there are "signs of life" that independent contributions could play a bigger role soon. METR found no bottlenecks that would slow the pace over the next twelve months, which means there's a "significant risk" that the acceleration will keep growing over the coming year.

blocks.text: Big uncertainty and dissenting voices

inlines.text: Big uncertainty and dissenting voices

blocks.text: METR also stresses how imprecise the results are. The true acceleration factor could be as low as 1.3 or as high as 3. When models from OpenAI, Google, and xAI are factored in, the industry-wide number drops to just 1.4, possibly because Anthropic lagged behind competitors in 2025 and a catch-up effect is skewing the figures.

blocks.text: Views inside Anthropic aren't uniform either. One researcher pegs AI's share of the productivity gains at just 15 to 20 percent and distrusts colleagues' self-reports. Another considers new hires the single most important factor of recent months.

blocks.text: Redacted evidence weakens the audit

inlines.text: Redacted evidence weakens the audit

blocks.text: Anthropic had unilateral redaction rights over all non-public information and used them heavily. According to METR, the majority of the evidence the auditors rated as most informative was stripped out, including forecasts for future models, breakdowns by training steps, and the bottleneck analysis. Anthropic describes the redactions as "aimed at removing confidential information that could accelerate other AI developers."

blocks.text: The result is that the public has to rely on METR's judgment "much more than would be ideal," the organization writes, and any talk of transparency around the evidence is off the table. One graph in METR's report accordingly features the words "FAKE DATA" in large letters.

blocks.text: Anthropic pulled the plug on a compute allocation audit

inlines.text: Anthropic pulled the plug on a compute allocation audit

blocks.text: In a companion review, METR also examines Anthropic's risk report from August 2026. In that report, the company publicly stated the acceleration was "less than a factor of 2." The internal, unredacted version implies a value of 1.97, though, and Anthropic itself calls it "plausible" that the threshold has been crossed. METR considers it possible that the warning level was already reached on July 15 and accuses the public report of understating both the acceleration and the uncertainty around it.
